newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-BOBBY UNSER SURVIVES MOUNTAIN ORDEAL.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BOBBY UNSER SURVIVES MOUNTAIN ORDEAL.

text.p: Three-time Indianapolis 500 winner Bobby Unser and a friend emerged unscathed on Sunday, surviving nearly 36 hours on a freezing Colorado mountain after their snowmobiles broke down.
Unser, 63, and Robert Gayton, 36, battled exhaustion, hypothermia and frostbite but managed to dig a snow cave for shelter and walk 14 miles (22 km) to safety through waist-deep snow.
The two men began their snowmobiling trip on Friday morning, but Gayton's snowmobile got stuck and Unser's developed engine problems.

They survived Friday night by digging into the snow under a tree, covering it with branches, building a roof of snow and crawling inside. The following morning, facing huge snowdrifts and falling into snow-covered creeks, Unser and Gayton used a compass and their wits to eventually find a barn with a telephone.
"We knew that if we quit, then it was quits," said Gayton, an Albuquerque mechanic. "Hopefully, this is a once in a lifetime experience."
"Everything that usually happens easy just kept getting worse," said Unser, an experienced snowmobiler whose knowledge of the San Juan Mountains helped the two men escape.
